name: Africa Center for Inclusive Development (ACID-Ghana)
title: Developing an Integrated Urban Climate, Disaster Risk and Infrastructure Resilience Platform for Secondary Cities in Ghana  This project seeks to co-develop an innovative digital decision-support platform that integrates meteorological information, climate projections, disaster risk data, geospatial technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and urban infrastructure datasets to improve resilience in Ghana's rapidly growing secondary cities. The platform will enable municipal authorities to identify climate and disaster hotspots, predict infrastructure vulnerabilities, strengthen early warning systems, prioritize resilient infrastructure investments, and support evidence-based urban planning. The research will combine interdisciplinary expertise in climate science, engineering, geospatial analytics, urban planning, and governance with local knowledge from municipalities and communities. Through co-creation with researchers and practice partners, the project will generate scalable tools, policy recommendations, and capacity-building approaches that enhance climate adaptation, disaster preparedness, and sustainable urban development in Ghana and other rapidly urbanizing cities in sub-Saharan Africa.
summary: Rapid urbanization and climate change are increasing the exposure of Ghana's secondary cities to flooding, heatwaves, infrastructure failures, and other climate-related disasters. Municipal authorities often lack integrated systems that combine weather information, disaster risk data, infrastructure inventories, and socioeconomic information to support proactive planning and emergency response. This project will co-develop an Integrated Urban Climate, Disaster Risk and Infrastructure Resilience Platform that uses AI, geospatial technologies, meteorological data, and infrastructure analytics to improve urban decision-making. Working with ETH researchers, municipal authorities, and national agencies, the project will develop predictive risk models, interactive dashboards, and decision-support tools for resilient infrastructure planning and disaster preparedness. Success will be measured by improved municipal capacity, enhanced early warning systems, better prioritization of infrastructure investments, strengthened inter-agency collaboration, and the adoption of the platform as a practical tool for climate-resilient urban governance in Ghana's secondary cities.
keywords: Urban Climate Resilience Disaster Risk Management Sustainable Urban Infrastructure Artificial Intelligence and Geospatial Analytics Urban Governance
rationale: Developing an integrated urban climate and infrastructure resilience platform requires interdisciplinary research expertise that extends beyond routine project implementation. We need a researcher to design robust methodologies, integrate meteorological, geospatial, infrastructure, and socioeconomic datasets, develop AI-based predictive models, and rigorously evaluate the platform's effectiveness. Research is also essential to validate climate risk models, assess infrastructure vulnerability under different scenarios, and generate evidence that can inform urban policy and investment decisions. This collaboration will ensure that the platform is scientifically robust, scalable, and capable of delivering measurable improvements in climate resilience and disaster risk management.
role: As the practice partner, the Africa Center for Inclusive Development (ACID-Ghana) will lead stakeholder engagement, coordinate implementation with municipal authorities and national agencies, facilitate community participation, and ensure that research outputs address real urban challenges. ACID-Ghana will provide access to field sites, local networks, implementation experience, and operational support for data collection, pilot testing, and capacity-building activities. We will also support knowledge exchange, policy engagement, and dissemination to promote uptake of the project's findings. Our ideal research partner would contribute expertise in urban systems, climate science, meteorology, geospatial analysis, artificial intelligence, infrastructure resilience, and impact evaluation. Together, we will co-design research activities, translate scientific evidence into practical decision-support tools, and develop scalable solutions that strengthen climate-resilient urban planning and infrastructure management in Ghana's secondary cities.

name: GridX d.o.o.
title: Drone-based detection of illegal construction for municipal urban governance
summary: Informal and illegal construction is a persistent governance failure across Western Balkan cities. Municipal inspectorates rely on slow, selective manual site visits and outdated cadastral records, so enforcement is reactive — often catching violations only after buildings are finished. This erodes public revenue, distorts urban planning, and produces unsafe, unregulated housing stock. This project pilots a drone-based, AI-assisted change-detection system that compares repeat aerial surveys against cadastral and permit data to flag unauthorized construction as it happens, not months or years later. Working with a municipal cadastre or inspectorate as practice partner, the pilot tests detection accuracy, false-positive rates, and — critically — whether staff can act on alerts within existing legal and administrative workflows. Success looks like a validated detection pipeline, a governance model municipalities can actually adopt, and evidence to support a follow-on Urban Research Grant scaling across multiple cities in Kosovo, North Macedonia, or Bosnia and Herzegovina.
keywords: informal construction, urban governance, AI change detection
rationale: GridX operates drones and produces mapping data at scale, but lacks the methodological rigor to validate a detection system a municipality can trust and adopt. We need a researcher to design the change-detection algorithm and accuracy benchmarks, structure a defensible evaluation of false-positive and false-negative rates against ground truth, and translate results into a governance framework municipal staff can act on. A consultant could build a working prototype; only academic research produces the independent, peer-reviewable evidence base that gives a public authority confidence to change its enforcement process.
role: GridX would be the non-academic practice partner, providing operational and local-access capability: drone flight operations and repeat aerial survey data over target sites; existing relationships with Serbian municipal authorities, cadastre offices, and infrastructure clients that give credible access to a pilot city and its inspectorate team; imagery-processing and mapping pipelines we already run commercially; and in-kind staff time, equipment, and flight hours as matching support. Our ideal ETH-domain researcher would bring geospatial/remote-sensing methodology, computer vision or machine learning expertise for automated change detection, and experience translating technical outputs into governance frameworks usable by public institutions.

name: Phenikaa University
title: AI-Enabled Urban Flood Resilience: A Digital Twin Approach for Hanoi
summary:
As Hanoi continues to grow and experiences more frequent and intense rainfall, urban flooding has become an increasingly serious challenge. Flood events disrupt transportation networks, affect essential public services, and place significant pressure on vulnerable communities. To address these challenges, this project proposes the development of an AI-enabled urban flood resilience platform that can support real-time flood forecasting, infrastructure planning, and emergency decision-making.

The project brings together several complementary technologies, including satellite remote sensing, IoT-based hydrological monitoring, machine learning, and a city-scale digital twin, to provide a clearer understanding of flood risks across Hanoi. These tools will be used to identify flood-prone areas, assess potential impacts on critical infrastructure, and test different adaptation strategies, such as smart drainage operations and nature-based flood mitigation measures.

A key feature of the project is its collaborative approach. The platform will be developed in close partnership with local authorities, infrastructure managers, and technology providers to ensure that the solutions are practical, relevant, and aligned with local needs. Outcomes will include a pilot flood resilience dashboard for Hanoi, more accurate flood forecasting capabilities, and evidence-based recommendations for infrastructure investments. The project will also promote stakeholder engagement and produce a scalable framework that can be adapted for other cities in Vietnam and across Southeast Asia that face similar climate-related flooding challenges.
keywords: Urban flood resilience, Climate adaptation, Digital twin, AI-based forecasting, Smart urban infrastructure
rationale: A researcher is crucial because the project requires scientific expertise, local contextual knowledge, and continuous stakeholder engagement. Researchers co-develop the methodology, integrate satellite, hydrological, and urban infrastructure data, validate AI forecasting models, and ensure that the digital twin reflects real flood conditions in Hanoi. They also bridge the gap between academic innovation and practical implementation by working with city authorities, communities, and technology partners. Their role is essential for generating reliable evidence, adapting solutions to local needs, evaluating impacts, and producing scalable knowledge and tools that can support long-term urban flood resilience beyond the pilot phase.
role: As part of this collaboration, I envision serving as the local principal investigator and coordination lead at Phenikaa University. I will contribute expertise in AI, remote sensing, GIS, and urban environmental data analysis to co-develop the flood resilience methodology and digital twin platform. My role will include coordinating data collection, engaging with local authorities and community stakeholders, supervising pilot implementation in Hanoi, and facilitating collaboration between academic researchers and Phenikaa’s technology ecosystem (including Phenikaa-X and related innovation units). I will also support capacity building, joint publications, dissemination activities, and the development of scalable solutions that can be transferred to other Vietnamese and Southeast Asian cities facing increasing urban flood risks under climate change.

name: Salalabs
title: We are designing and operating SLink - a framework for network of urban mobility/logistics hubs to reduce congestion, emissions and last-mile costs in rapidly growing Vietnamese cities.
summary:
Project: Data-Driven Mobility Hubs for Sustainable Last-Mile Logistics in Vietnam

1. Problem Statements
Walk through any ward in HCMC or Hanoi at 5pm. You'll see 3 problems at once:
- Car/Motorbikes double-parking on sidewalks, blocking traffic and pedestrians.
- Inconvenience to shifting to electric-bike/car with various joining manufactures but no standards or charging hubs
- Vans and trucks circling the block 20 minutes to find a place to drop 50 parcels, burning fuel and causing congestion.
- Customers waiting at home all day, then getting 3 missed-delivery notices because no one was there.

This happens 10 million times per month. Individual Vehicles still increasing, E-commerce in Vietnam grew 25% last year, but our streets and buildings were not designed for this volume.
Right now, no safe sidewalks or green/logistics hubs. If we keep pushing vehicles, services, building to the market but without spatial space for hubs or valid data, we'll just add more traffic, more emissions, and more wasted time.

2. Who is Affected
- Citizens: Lose time to traffic, breathe dirtier air, and lose sidewalk space to parked cars/motobikes. Inconvenience barrier to go with e-bikes without worrying about incompatible public charger but keeping purchasing gasoline motorbikes.
- Cities: Fail to meet climate and congestion targets. Roads get damaged faster. Planning departments have no tools to manage "logistics" as urban infrastructure. Unable to achieve the net-zero target and sustainable urban development.
- SLink + drivers: Pay higher fuel costs, lower pay per trip, and get blamed for congestion/dirty air. Hubs are under-utilised because we don’t know the best location or operating hours.

3. Objectives of the Project
- Mobility: Cut last-mile vehicle trips and emissions by making deliveries smarter and closer to the customer. Ease to find a peace/green space with utilised services among the chaotic commute.
- Spatial Planning: Use data to put the right hub in the right place, so goods move through the city, not around it.
- Policy: Give Vietnamese cities the first-ever evidence-based guidelines to plan transport/logistics hub as part of urban infrastructure.

4. Proposed Approach
An ETH Zurich + SLink consortium in 3 pilot Vietnamese cities.
- On the Ground Data: SLink provides real-time data from hubs: Data for ESG indexes, parcel volume, timing, failed deliveries, driver routes.
- ETH Research: Develop AI tools for hub location optimization, demand forecasting, and dynamic PUDO scheduling.
- Test & Learn: Deploy the tools in live hubs. Work with city People's Committees to measure impact on traffic and emissions.
- Scale: Publish an "Sustainable Urban Transport and Logistics Hub Playbook" for other SECO partner countries.

5. What SLink Hopes to Achieve / What Success Looks Like
- For People: Parcels arrive faster, with fewer trucks on the street. Remove Car/Motorbikes double-parking on sidewalks. Clean Air. Consumers can pick up near their home in 15 minutes.
- For Cities: Security of space for sidewalks. Acceleration of Net-zero/ESG targets. A 15% reduction in last-mile delivery Vehicle-kilometers and CO2 in pilot areas. Logistics is finally included in the city masterplan.
- For SLink: 20% higher hub utilization and 10% lower cost per services. We prove that proper hub-distribution/logistics infrastructure can make cities better, not worse.
- For SECO/ETH: A replicable, data-driven model for sustainable urban transportation/logistics in emerging markets.

Summary: We want to turn thousands of SLink hubs from "Urban spatial hub" into "Intelligent infrastructure" that makes Vietnamese cities cleaner, faster, and more livable.
keywords: Sustainable Last-mile, Urban Mobility, Green Spatial Space, Micro-Logistics Hubs, Data-Drive Infrastructure
rationale: We don't have a scientific method to plan logistics infrastructure that balances commercial viability with urban sustainability. Rigorous research can turn SLink's hubs from reactive sites into a predictive city-scale infrastructure network.
role: We can provide exclusive data access of live network to hubs, plus operational expertise/support (ground truth) to validate and scale research findings in Vietnam.

name: Posts and Telecommunications Institute of Technology
title: AI-Integrated Multi-UAV System for Real-Time Disaster Monitoring, Victim Detection and Localization, and Search-and-Rescue Support
summary:
Annually, Vietnam faces numerous disasters, particularly large-scale storms, floods, fires, and explosions across residential, urban, and industrial areas. These events cause severe loss of life and property and significantly affect infrastructure, communities, and the environment. This project aims to develop a technological solution that enables search-and-rescue teams to rapidly assess disaster sites, reach affected areas, and assist victims. It is intended to support local authorities and provide a comprehensive platform for organizations involved in emergency response.

The proposed system combines UAVs, software, AI, and continuous communication to enable seamless coordination among command centers, reconnaissance units, and field rescue teams. It will provide real-time situational awareness through digitally reconstructed maps, automatically detect and geolocate victims, analyze hazards, and recommend feasible access and rescue strategies. Success would mean enabling faster decision-making, reducing response times, improving coordination, and helping rescue teams reach victims and damaged structures as quickly and safely as possible.
keywords: Disaster resilience, AI-enabled UAVs, Emergency response, Victim localization, Real-time situational awareness
rationale: Having grown up in a mountainous district frequently affected by storms, flash floods, and landslides, and having personally supported rescue efforts during fire incidents, I understand the challenges faced by affected communities and emergency responders. I have already implemented several local support solutions, but a gap remains between research algorithms and systems that can operate reliably under real disaster conditions. I need a researcher to help rigorously validate, evaluate, and improve the system. The fund’s support would enable us to combine research expertise with practical field experience and develop a reliable solution that can be scaled to support more communities.
role: If the project moves forward, I will serve as project lead, taking responsibility for planning, requirements definition, system design, implementation, stakeholder coordination, and evaluation. I will work with local authorities and rescue organizations to understand location-specific needs while ensuring that the solution remains adaptable to different disaster environments. The ideal researcher would contribute expertise in multi-UAV systems, computer vision, victim detection and localization, environmental reconstruction, optimization, modelling, and experimental evaluation. I can contribute expertise in software development, AI model and system optimization, computing and communication infrastructure, technical personnel, operational knowledge, collected data, simulation environments, and access to field-testing sites. I will also coordinate dataset development, organize simulations and field experiments, analyze results, and translate research methods into a reliable operational prototype. Through this collaboration, I aim to bridge scientific innovation and practical deployment, ensuring that the system is technically robust, field-relevant, scalable, and suitable for long-term adoption by emergency-response organizations.

name: Vietnam Maritime University
title: Enhancing Intermodal and Port–Hinterland Connectivity for Low-Carbon Freight Transport in Hai Phong
summary: Connecting goods between Hai Phong port and industrial parks, logistics centers and back-end markets is still highly dependent on roads, while railways, inland waterways and transshipment points have not been effectively integrated. This increases transit times, logistics costs, congestion, emissions, and traffic risks. Import-export enterprises, shipping companies, port operators, people along logistics corridors and management agencies are all affected. The competitiveness of Hai Phong port, supply chain efficiency, urban environmental quality and emission reduction goals are therefore threatened. The project will map the flow of goods, identify bottlenecks, evaluate intermodal transport scenarios and propose infrastructure, operation and coordination solutions. Success is a priority roadmap and pilot solution that can be measured, applied, and replicated.
keywords: intermodal transport, port-hinderland connectivity, low-carbon city
rationale: There is currently no integrated database showing how and where goods are transported from Hai Phong port to industrial parks, logistics centers and the back-end market, where waiting times arise, empty vehicles, inefficient transshipment and high emissions. The data is currently scattered at ports, transport enterprises and management agencies, so it is not enough to objectively compare road, railway and inland waterway options. The researcher is needed to build baselines, model networks, evaluate modal shift scenarios, and design a pilot solution with clear measurement indicators.
role: We are expected to be the research partner and coordinating focal point in Hai Phong. The team will work with ETH partners to identify research questions, select priority port-rear corridors, develop data collection methods, and co-design pilot solutions. We will review policies and planning, conduct field surveys, interview businesses, consult with regulators, and support access to ports, industrial parks, logistics centers, and related transport routes. The team can contribute local networks, understanding of Vietnam's port and logistics systems, research personnel, expert time, work locations, and workshop support. The ideal research partner should have expertise in GIS, network analysis, intermodal transport modeling, logistics optimization, emissions calculations, and impact assessment. The two sides will jointly analyze data, test solutions, evaluate results and build a roadmap for replication.

name: Environmental Chemistry and Ecotoxicology Lab, Phenikaa University
title: Assessment and Sustainable Treatment of Water Pollution Associated with Plastic Waste Leakage in Urban and Coastal Areas of Vietnam
summary:
This project aims to assess the extent of water pollution associated with plastic waste leakage, with a particular focus on microplastics, organic pollutants, heavy metals, and antibiotic-resistant microorganisms in urban waterways, drainage canals, and coastal environments in Vietnam. Building on the objectives of the Less Plastic Vietnam initiative, the project will identify pollution hotspots, investigate the distribution and transport of microplastics, and evaluate their interactions with other contaminants in water and sediment systems.

In parallel, the project will develop and pilot sustainable treatment solutions, including biochar and other bio-based adsorbent materials derived from agricultural residues, as well as constructed wetland systems combining aquatic plants and beneficial microorganisms for the removal of microplastics and associated pollutants from wastewater and surface water.

The expected outcomes include: (i) a comprehensive database on plastic-related water pollution, (ii) cost-effective and environmentally friendly water treatment technologies, (iii) pilot-scale demonstration models, and (iv) policy recommendations to support plastic waste reduction, water quality protection, and the transition toward a circular economy and sustainable urban development in Vietnam.
keywords: Microplastic pollution,  Water quality assessment, Sustainable wastewater treatment , Urban and coastal water management, Circular economy and plastic waste reduction
rationale: A researcher is crucial because the project requires scientific expertise to design reliable sampling strategies, analyze microplastics and associated contaminants, and evaluate treatment performance using evidence-based methods. Researchers also connect laboratory findings with real environmental conditions, work with local stakeholders to identify pollution hotspots, and ensure that the proposed treatment technologies are technically feasible, environmentally sustainable, and scalable. Their role is essential for generating credible data, guiding decision-making, and transforming the project from a monitoring activity into a practical solution that supports plastic waste reduction and long-term water quality improvement in Vietnam
role: As part of this collaboration, I envision serving as the local project coordinator and research lead at Phenikaa University. I will contribute expertise in environmental monitoring, microplastic analysis, water quality assessment, and sustainable treatment technologies, while coordinating field sampling, laboratory analysis, and stakeholder engagement with local authorities and community partners. I will also facilitate collaboration between ECET Lab, Phenikaa’s interdisciplinary research groups, and international partners to develop pilot-scale treatment solutions and joint research outputs. In addition, I will support student and researcher exchange, capacity building, data sharing, scientific publications, and dissemination activities to ensure that the project generates both strong scientific outcomes and practical impacts for water pollution reduction and sustainable environmental management in Vietnam.

name: Vina Hydrogen Co., Ltd.
title: Development and Demonstration of Honeycomb Plasma Catalyst Technology for Advanced Air Purification
summary:
Vina Hydrogen Co., Ltd. (VINA-H) has developed an innovative honeycomb plasma catalyst technology for advanced air purification. Laboratory-scale testing demonstrated the effective removal of hydrogen, ammonia, and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) at ppm levels under ambient conditions, including high-humidity environments. Catalyst-coated honeycomb structures significantly enhance pollutant conversion efficiency, offering superior performance compared with conventional systems.
Unlike existing air purifiers that primarily remove particulate matter, this technology simultaneously eliminates hazardous gases, dust, and airborne microorganisms, providing a safer and healthier indoor environment.
This joint research project will design, fabricate, and validate plasma catalyst air purification systems of various capacities for pilot demonstrations in Vietnam. The project will optimize reactor design and manufacturing processes to reduce production costs while ensuring high efficiency, durability, and operational reliability. Successful commercialization will provide an affordable, high-performance air purification solution for industrial, commercial, and public facilities.
keywords: Plasma, VOCs Removal, Advanced Air Purification, Hydrogen
rationale: A researcher is crucial to the successful co-development and implementation of the Honeycomb Plasma Catalyst Technology project by providing scientific expertise in plasma engineering, catalyst design, reactor optimization, and air quality analysis. They also bridge laboratory research with pilot-scale demonstration, solve technical challenges, analyze performance data, and collaborate with industry partners to accelerate commercialization. Their expertise is essential for developing an innovative, reliable, and scalable air purification technology with measurable environmental and public health benefits.
role: I envision playing a leading role in the technical development, demonstration, and future commercialization of the Honeycomb Plasma Catalyst Technology for Advanced Air Purification. My responsibilities will include designing and optimizing the plasma-catalyst reactor, planning and conducting laboratory and pilot-scale experiments, evaluating pollutant removal performance, and analyzing experimental data. I will also coordinate collaboration among research institutions, industry partners, and end users to ensure the technology addresses real-world environmental challenges. In addition, I will contribute to project management, mentor junior researchers, publish scientific outcomes, and support intellectual property development and commercialization strategies. By combining my expertise in plasma technologies, hydrogen systems, and technology transfer, I aim to help transform this innovative research into a practical, scalable, and market-ready solution that improves air quality and delivers lasting environmental and societal benefits.

name: National Agency for Scientific Research Promotion
countries: Albania; Egypt; Czech Republic; Hungary; Morocco; Poland; South Africa; Vietnam; Uzbekistan; Tunisia; Tajikistan
title: Advancing Water Security and Climate Resilience through Innovation and Technology Transfer in the Mediterranean
summary:
Across the Mediterranean, particularly in Tunisia and other water-stressed countries, communities, farmers, industries and public authorities are increasingly affected by water scarcity, droughts, climate change and inefficient water management. Declining water availability threatens food security, economic activities, ecosystems and the well-being of local communities.

The project aims to strengthen water security and climate resilience by connecting research, innovation and real-world needs. It will identify common challenges, map and assess innovative water technologies, and pilot practical solutions for water efficiency, wastewater reuse, smart monitoring, sustainable agriculture and climate adaptation. A strong focus will be placed on technology transfer, capacity building and cooperation between research institutions, public authorities and businesses.

Success will mean measurable improvements in water efficiency, increased reuse of water resources, successful technology transfer, stronger research–industry collaboration, and scalable solutions that can be replicated across Mediterranean countries.
keywords: Water Scarcity – Climate Adaptation – Smart Water Management – Technology Transfer – Mediterranean Cooperation
rationale: A researcher is crucial to ensure that the project is based on robust scientific evidence and responds to real water challenges. Research can identify the underlying causes of water scarcity, assess the effectiveness and sustainability of innovative technologies, and generate reliable data to guide decisions. Researchers can also adapt solutions to local Mediterranean contexts, evaluate their environmental, economic and social impacts, and develop evidence-based indicators to measure results. Their involvement will bridge the gap between scientific knowledge and practical implementation, while facilitating knowledge exchange and technology transfer between research institutions, public authorities and businesses. This scientific approach will help ensure that solutions are effective, scalable and replicable.
role: As ANPR, we envision a role as a national facilitator and bridge between researchers, public authorities, businesses and other stakeholders in Tunisia and the wider Mediterranean region. We would contribute our experience in research and innovation programme management, technology transfer, stakeholder engagement and international cooperation. We can provide access to relevant national networks, research institutions, public stakeholders and potential pilot sites, as well as facilitate data collection and field activities. We would support the identification of local water challenges, co-design and implementation of pilot actions, dissemination of results and scaling of successful solutions. The ideal researcher would bring expertise in water management, climate modelling, technology assessment, impact evaluation and evidence-based approaches. Together, we aim to connect scientific knowledge with local needs and accelerate the adoption of practical, scalable and sustainable water solutions.

name: Local Government Service (Wassa East District Assembly)
title: The project builds in an empirical study I did in 2024/2025 on how transport systems have functionally facilitated the development of The Sekondi-Takoradi Urban Network, one of the 11 proposed polycentric urban regions in the Ghana National Spatial Development Framework (2015 - 2035). The current proposal is to partner with researchers in Switzerland and South Africa to do a comparative study on user centered transport systems.
summary: Despite a polycentric spatial policy and a national transport framework that envision integrated, multimodal mass commuting across eleven designated urban networks, public transportation in Ghana remains inefficient and especially disadvantages those living at the urban edge. These shortcomings limit access to jobs, services, and opportunities to participate in urban life, while simultaneously reinforcing reliance on private vehicles for efficient travel and sprawling urban edges. Focusing on the Sekondi-Takoradi Urban Network, this study investigates how mass transit models often drawn from Global North contexts are reshaped to address end-user commuting patterns. A comparative lens encompassing a proposed network in Switzerland and Johannesburg, South Africa, will help identify principles for more context-sensitive transport planning. This empirical and comparative study will deliver evidence-based recommendations for user-centred principles in the design and development of mass commuting infrastructure, transforming public transport into a more attractive, efficient, respectable and socially accepted substitute for private car use for all social classes. Through this partnership, we believe accessibility in the metropolis can be improved through evidence-based strategies.
keywords: Public transport, user-centred design, multimodal networks, Sekondi-Takoradi,
rationale: Undertaking a comparative, multi-context study requires specialised research capacity, an understanding of  normative theory, and the ability to facilitate a neutral study that contrasts user centred design in Europe and African. While I have an interest in a comparative study, I do not have the research skills and knowledge of the methods, data and analysis for this project. Moreover, since most of the mass commuting policy and projects are inspired by global north paradigms, a researcher from this context will be better placed to objectively lead our comparative study.
role: This project builds directly on findings from my earlier research, which evaluated how public transport can support the implementation of a polycentric urban system. My role as a planner in the local government service and municipality provides practical access to government-designated officials for data and interviews. I can also facilitate focus group discussions, stakeholder interviews, and the engagement of specialised experts in Ghana where needed. Finally, I am positioned to help translate the research findings and recommendations into metropolitan transport plans and policies..

name: Zeri i Zanatit
title: Remote Work, Infrastructure and Talent Retention in Albania's Secondary Cities
summary:
Albania's labour market debate focuses on emigration, but an equally important pattern is internal migration toward Tirana. Many remote-capable professionals move to the capital not because their work requires it but because secondary cities lack infrastructure and services — healthcare, education, connectivity, and public workspace to support a full professional life. 

Our project, building on an existing validated media platform (11 published interviews with professionals nationwide), investigates under what infrastructure and remote-work conditions professionals would prefer to stay in or return to secondary cities rather than relocate to Tirana. Using 24 structured qualitative interviews alongside labour-market and economic data from local partners, we aim to identify which infrastructure investments most effectively convert remote-work potential into actual talent retention. Success looks like an evidence-based framework that helps secondary cities prioritise investments that reduce migration pressure on the capital and support more balanced urban development.
keywords: urban development, internal migration, remote work, talent retention, secondary cities
rationale: While our media platform has direct access to professionals across Albania and has already gathered valuable qualitative material, we lack the rigorous research design, sampling methodology, and analytical framework needed to turn these stories into credible evidence. A researcher would help us design a defensible qualitative methodology, ensure the study can distinguish genuine patterns from anecdote, and connect our findings to existing urban-migration and labour-market literature. Day-to-day production can capture individual stories, but it cannot on its own produce a triangulated, policy-relevant framework linking remote work, infrastructure gaps, and migration decisions, which is exactly the kind of synthesis this project needs.
role: I would lead the Albania-side team and field research: identifying and interviewing 24 professionals across diverse secondary cities, professions, ages and genders, coordinating local academic and practice partners (economics and labour-market perspectives), and translating findings into accessible public content that also serves as dissemination. I bring an already-validated media platform with direct access to professionals nationwide (11 published interviews, ~21,000 organic views, ~2M impressions), established relationships with entrepreneurs and freelancers across different regions, and the capacity to conduct and produce structured interviews at scale.  From the researcher, I'm looking for expertise in qualitative or mixed-methods research design, migration/urban-economics framing, and guidance on turning interview data into a rigorous, triangulated evidence base, as well as support shaping a research question that genuinely serves both scientific and practical goals.

name: Institute of Urban Planning and Development Research
title: Enhancing Community Capacity for Flood Prevention and Climate Change Response in the Urban Centre of Thai [removed], Thai [removed] Province
summary: Thái [removed]’s urban centre faces increasing risks from heavy rainfall, flooding, and climate-related extreme weather, affecting residents, infrastructure, and local socio-economic activities. The community remains constrained by limited awareness, knowledge, preparedness, response skills, access to early-warning information, and coordination capacity, while local authorities also face limitations in community-based disaster risk management. The project aims to assess community capacity, identify vulnerable groups and areas, analyse factors affecting resilience, and develop practical solutions for proactive flood preparedness, response, and recovery. The proposed approach combines theoretical and practical assessment, community surveys, participatory risk mapping, workshops and training, development of an early-warning communication process, and pilot testing of a community-led flood preparedness model. Success will be reflected in improved community capacity, practical guidance and training materials, a replicable toolkit, and a tested model that can be adapted by other localities facing similar risks.
keywords: Community Capacity , Flood Risk Management , Climate Change Adaptation ,Community-Based Disaster Risk Management ,Community Resilience
rationale: A researcher is crucial to bridge local practice with rigorous, internationally informed research. Our Institute has strong expertise and networks in urban planning, community participation and climate change adaptation in Vietnam. Collaboration with a Swiss research partner can help Vietnam access advanced knowledge, methods and relevant international experience, while strengthening the research capacity of Vietnamese professionals through internationally recognised approaches. Joint research can provide robust evidence to design and evaluate the pilot before wider replication, identify practical improvements, and generate lessons for strengthening mechanisms and policies for local authorities. By sharing knowledge, expertise and other resources, both partners can develop a scientifically grounded and context-sensitive model with greater feasibility, credibility and potential for wider application.
role: As a Vietnamese research partner under the Vietnam Urban Planning and Development Association (VUPDA), our Institute will connect international research expertise with local implementation. We will facilitate engagement with Thai [removed] authorities and communities, provide access to relevant urban planning, climate change and flood-risk data, and support field research, participatory activities, training and pilot implementation. Our professional members have experience in urban planning, community participation and climate change adaptation, as well as international development projects supported by the World Bank, ADB, KOICA and the Ford Foundation. We will contribute professional networks, field access, staff time, technical expertise and local knowledge. Through collaboration with the Swiss partner, we aim to strengthen Vietnamese researchers’ capacity in internationally recognised research methods, share knowledge and resources, and jointly evaluate the pilot to ensure its feasibility before scaling up. The partnership will also generate evidence and practical recommendations to support improvements in local disaster-risk management mechanisms and policies.

name: Viet Nam Sustainable City Development Joint Stock Company
title: PROJECT TITLE: Application of Green Infrastructure Solutions in Designing Green Spaces in the Northern Area of Hue Central City (Hue Citadel) with Community Participation
summary:
Problem Statement: Severe inner-city flooding, climate change, and high urban concretization threaten the UNESCO World Cultural Heritage site of the Hue Citadel. Heavy rainfall overloads silted historic hydrological networks. Conventional grey infrastructure conflicts with Heritage Conservation Laws, while local wards lack resources for community-driven flood mitigation. 
Objectives: The project aims to transform the heritage green space into a multifunctional Green Infrastructure (GI) framework to mitigate flooding, lower temperatures, and align with Net-Zero goals through community participation and heritage-sensitive design. 
Proposed Approach: The project integrates GIS spatial mapping, hydraulic modeling, Nature-based Solutions (NbS), and native plant species. It establishes a "Co-design & Co-management" framework, retrofitting cleared relocation zones and garden houses into stormwater management units. 
Vision of Success: Success looks like a restored, cohesive "Sponge Network", reduced flood risks via pilot GI models, active community co-management via the Hue-S platform, and established technical/policy guidelines for Heritage-Safe GI implementation.
keywords: Designing Green Spaces, Green Infrastructure (GI),Community Participation, Hue City's Greenery System
rationale: Co-developing with an ETH Domain researcher is crucial to access world-class research capacity in urban development, infrastructure, and climate resilience. Day-to-day operations and consultants lack the interdisciplinary depth needed to bridge Green Infrastructure with strict UNESCO heritage conservation. Through this partnership, we will get innovative analytics, digital tools, GIS methodologies, and technical prototype designs for sponge-city infrastructure. We require the researcher’s specialized skills in hydraulic flow modeling, climate-resilient NbS design , and participatory frameworks to transform Hue's historical water network safely.
role: Conducts topographic surveys, mapping, cadastral measurements, and land inventories. Prepares investment reports and cost estimates, performs technical design and verification for civil/infrastructure engineering, and manages project supervision and legal compliance. Leads spatial planning, heritage-sensitive landscape design, and eco-friendly Green Infrastructure (GI) solutions. Facilitates community co-design workshops, conducts urban social research, develops community-led maintenance frameworks, and manages capacity building and scientific dissemination.

name: Center for Durable Solution Dialogue (CDSD)
title: Developing and Testing Innovative and Scalable Solutions for Ukraine’s Urban Recovery
summary: Ukraine’s cities face an extraordinary urban recovery challenge: mass displacement, damaged infrastructure, changing demographics and constrained municipal resources are reshaping demand for housing, services and urban development. CDSD recently led a nationwide study, supported by international partners including the UN and INGOs, drawing on evidence from over 700 local self-government units. The research identified systemic challenges in municipal planning, housing and asset management, financing, data, transparency and institutional capacity, and recommended pathways for addressing them. These findings and recommendations provide the evidence base for this proposal. With recovery high on national and international agendas and major legislative reforms underway, practical, modern solutions are urgently needed. We seek to partner with ETH researchers to develop and test innovative and scalable approaches to housing provision and management, public asset management, urban planning and financing, including digital and blockchain-enabled governance. Success means tested tools, policies or prototypes that municipalities can adopt, complementing recovery efforts and unlocking opportunities for humanitarian and development investment.
keywords: Urban recovery; Municipal governance; Digital innovation; Public asset management; Sustainable financing
rationale: CDSD’s nationwide research identified systemic gaps in municipal asset records, transparency, housing management, financing and institutional capacity, alongside potential pathways for reform. We now seek expertise in decentralized digital infrastructure, smart contracts, verifiable asset registries, transparent value transfers and programmable governance to investigate whether these technologies can address such problems more effectively than conventional systems. Key questions include where decentralization genuinely adds value, how public assets and transactions can become traceable and auditable while protecting sensitive data, and how technology could improve municipal efficiency and accountability. We also seek to explore innovative financing mechanisms that can mobilise, channel and transparently manage investment for urban recovery.
role: CDSD offers an unusually strong platform for applied research in Ukraine: a substantial evidence base, access to the institutions that shape urban recovery, and the capacity to test solutions in real-world conditions. Our team brings 25 years of experience addressing displacement and housing challenges across Ukraine and nearly a dozen other crisis contexts, including 11 continuous years in Ukraine. Most recently, we led nationwide research engaging over 700 local self-government units and examining three decades of Ukrainian housing policy, legislation, programmes and delivery models. This provides both a deep understanding of systemic constraints and a strong foundation for testing alternatives. Our established relationships with municipalities, national authorities, and humanitarian and development partners can provide pathways from research to piloting, policy uptake and scale, while our Ukraine-based team can operate throughout the conflict. We seek complementary ETH expertise in digital infrastructure, systems design, modelling, urban planning and innovative financing to turn this foundation into rigorously tested solutions.

name: Global Sustainable Futures Network CIC
title: Alexandria Low-Carbon Mobility Corridor: Electrifying Microbuses and Transforming El-Gaish Road for People, Climate and Active Mobility
summary: Alexandria faces growing transport-related emissions, congestion and pressure on urban public space. El-Gaish Road, a major coastal corridor, presents an opportunity to demonstrate how transport electrification and people-centred urban design can be integrated into a low-carbon mobility model. The project will assess the feasibility of transitioning Alexandria’s microbus system towards electric mobility, including charging infrastructure, operational requirements, costs, emissions reductions and implementation pathways. In parallel, it will map and assess El-Gaish Road to identify opportunities for safer and more attractive walking and cycling, improved public transport integration, reduced car dependency and potential low-emission zones. Through stakeholder engagement, spatial and mobility analysis, emissions modelling and scenario development, the project will develop a practical pilot concept and investment-ready roadmap. Success would be a locally grounded, evidence-based model demonstrating measurable carbon reduction while improving accessibility, public space and quality of life.
keywords: Urban mobility; Transport electrification; Low-carbon cities; Active mobility; Climate-resilient urban planning
rationale: An ETH-domain researcher is crucial to develop robust, research-based evidence for transforming Alexandria’s urban mobility system. We need rigorous analysis to quantify the potential carbon, air-quality, mobility and social impacts of microbus electrification and alternative street-use scenarios for El-Gaish Road. The researcher would bring expertise in transport systems, urban planning, spatial analysis, emissions modelling, scenario development and evaluation that goes beyond a conventional consultancy or operational assessment. This collaboration would enable us to test evidence-based pathways, identify what interventions are most effective and develop a scientifically credible, transferable model for low-carbon urban mobility.
role: We would contribute the practical, local and implementation perspective required to ensure the research responds to Alexandria’s real urban challenges. Our role would include supporting access to relevant local stakeholders, transport operators, municipal and planning actors, community representatives and other practitioners; facilitating field engagement and data collection; identifying relevant local datasets; and supporting mapping and assessment of El-Gaish Road and the microbus system.  We would also contribute project coordination, stakeholder engagement, contextual knowledge, dissemination and development of pathways for piloting and scaling the findings. Our networks can help connect the research team with Egyptian institutions and potential implementation partners.  Ideally, the ETH-domain researcher would contribute expertise in sustainable transport, electric mobility, urban systems, GIS/spatial analysis, emissions modelling, active mobility and impact evaluation, while we jointly develop the research methodology, pilot concept and implementation roadmap.

name: Global Sustainable Futures Network CIC
title: Cocoa Circular Energy: Developing a Decentralised Waste-to-Energy Model for 25,000 Cocoa Farmers in Ghana
summary: Cocoa production generates significant volumes of organic residues that are often underutilised, creating environmental challenges while rural communities face energy and income constraints. Working with a network of approximately 25,000 cocoa farmers in Ghana, the project will investigate how cocoa pod husks and other agricultural residues can be converted into useful energy and valuable bio-products through decentralised circular economy models. The research will quantify available biomass, assess appropriate conversion pathways, model energy and greenhouse-gas reduction potential, and evaluate economic, social and environmental impacts. It will also explore how farmer organisations, local enterprises and energy users could participate in viable value chains. The project will develop an evidence-based model and pilot framework for decentralised cocoa waste-to-energy systems that can reduce waste, improve energy access, create additional farmer value and contribute to Ghana’s low-carbon transition.
keywords: Waste-to-energy; Circular economy; Cocoa residues; Renewable energy; Low-carbon agriculture
rationale: An ETH-domain researcher is crucial to generate rigorous evidence on the technical, environmental, economic and social potential of converting cocoa residues into energy. Key knowledge gaps include the availability and seasonality of biomass, optimal conversion pathways, energy yields, lifecycle greenhouse-gas impacts, carbon mitigation potential and the viability of decentralised systems across farming communities. Research expertise in bioenergy systems, resource modelling, lifecycle assessment, spatial analysis and techno-economic evaluation would enable robust comparison of technology and deployment scenarios. This evidence is essential to move beyond a conventional consultancy assessment and develop a scientifically validated, scalable model for Ghana’s cocoa-producing communities.
role: We would provide the real-world field platform and implementation context for the research, including access to a network of approximately 25,000 cocoa farmers and relevant farmer organisations and local stakeholders in Ghana. We can facilitate field engagement, stakeholder consultations, data collection and validation of assumptions regarding cocoa production, residue generation, current waste practices and local energy needs.  Our team can support identification and mapping of cocoa-producing communities, coordinate engagement with farmers and local institutions, and contribute staff time, project coordination, communications and dissemination. We would also help identify potential sites and implementation partners for future pilot activities and explore pathways for scaling successful models.  The ETH-domain researcher would ideally contribute expertise in bioenergy, waste-to-energy systems, circular economy, lifecycle assessment, techno-economic modelling, spatial analysis and impact evaluation. Together, we would develop evidence-based scenarios and a scalable implementation and investment roadmap.

name: Arab Academy for Science and Technology and Maritime Transport (AASTMT)
title: Alexandria Low-Carbon Mobility Corridor: Electrifying Microbuses and Transforming El-Gaish Road for Sustainable Urban Mobility
summary: Alexandria faces increasing transport-related emissions, congestion and pressure on public space, while El-Gaish Road represents a major urban and coastal mobility corridor with significant potential for transformation. The project will develop a research-based pathway for transitioning Alexandria’s microbus system towards electric mobility while exploring how El-Gaish Road can become a more pedestrian- and bicycle-friendly, low-carbon urban corridor. AASTMT will work with an ETH-domain research partner to assess mobility patterns, transport emissions, electrification scenarios, charging requirements, active-mobility opportunities and alternative street-use configurations. The project will combine spatial analysis, transport and emissions modelling, stakeholder engagement and scenario development to identify technically, environmentally, socially and economically viable pathways. Success would be an evidence-based, locally grounded model and implementation roadmap demonstrating how transport electrification and people-centred urban design can reduce emissions while improving accessibility, safety and quality of life in Alexandria.
keywords: Sustainable urban mobility; Electric mobility; Low-carbon transport; Active mobility; Urban transformation
rationale: AASTMT seeks to develop robust research-based evidence to guide Alexandria’s transition towards low-carbon urban mobility. Important knowledge gaps include the real-world emissions and mobility impacts of microbus electrification, optimal charging and operating scenarios, and how changes to El-Gaish Road could affect walking, cycling, public transport, traffic and carbon emissions. An ETH-domain researcher would provide advanced expertise in sustainable transport, electric mobility, urban systems, GIS, transport and emissions modelling, scenario analysis and impact evaluation. This would enable rigorous comparison of alternative pathways and generate scientifically credible evidence to inform policy, investment and future implementation beyond what routine operational analysis or consultancy could provide.
role: AASTMT will provide the Egyptian academic, research and implementation platform for the collaboration, bringing expertise in maritime and transport systems, engineering, urban development and applied research. AASTMT can facilitate access to relevant transport, mobility and urban datasets and support engagement with municipal authorities, transport operators, planners, infrastructure stakeholders and local communities in Alexandria. AASTMT can contribute researchers, technical staff, student researchers and institutional facilities to support field investigations, data collection, GIS mapping, modelling, stakeholder engagement and validation of research findings. Its local knowledge and institutional networks will help ensure that the research reflects Alexandria’s specific mobility, infrastructure and socioeconomic conditions. The ETH-domain partner would ideally contribute complementary expertise in electric mobility, sustainable transport systems, urban planning, GIS/spatial analysis, emissions modelling, active mobility and impact evaluation. Together, AASTMT and the ETH partner would co-develop the methodology, scenarios, pilot concept and evidence-based roadmap for implementation and scaling.

name: Public Union "Taste route of Prykarpattia"
topic: Preservation and Sustainable Use of Wild Plants in the Carpathians
title: Carpathian Craft & Superfood Cluster: Sustainable Harvesting and Product Innovation
summary:
Small farmers in the Carpathian region face economic instability and lack of the technology to transform rich local resources into high-value goods. Without structured processing, sustainable harvesting methods, and strong market access, valuable ecosystem potential is lost, while local livelihoods remain fragile.

This project bridges Swiss R&D expertise with local Carpathian producers to build a resilient, value-added agro-food ecosystem. We will establish sustainable harvesting protocols for wild plants, develop innovative packaged superfoods (such as fruit jellies, candied fruits, and natural sweets), and strengthen the regional cluster and cooperative movement.

By combining scientific processing with collaborative farmer networks, we aim to transform raw local resources into market-ready products. Success will be defined by higher farmer incomes, preserved Carpathian biodiversity, and a scalable cooperative model for local craft producers.
keywords: Agro-food Innovation  Sustainable Harvesting  Craft Production  Cooperative Development  Local Superfoods
rationale: We face a knowledge gap in biochemical standardization, bio-resource modeling, and shelf-life optimization for wild-sourced superfoods. An ETH Zurich researcher brings world-class expertise in sustainable food processing engineering and bio-resource management. Beyond short-term consultancy, rigorous ETH research will establish scientific harvesting limits to protect biodiversity while optimizing precise extraction and processing formulas for high-value products (like candied fruits and natural sweets), enabling a scientifically backed, scalable cluster model.
role: As a regional hub, we provide direct access to an extensive local network of smallholder farmers, wild plant gatherers, and artisanal producers. We offer authentic field sites across the Carpathian region, historical local recipes, primary raw material samples, and operational staff time for pilot testing. Additionally, we provide full on-the-ground logistical support, stakeholder facilitation, and in-kind contributions to bridge academic research with practical, market-driven cluster execution.

name: Department of economic development, Lviv city council
title: Evidence-Based Economic Transformation of a Resilient City: Developing a Data-Driven Economic Development Research for Lviv
summary:
Lviv is undergoing a profound economic transformation driven by the war in Ukraine, population displacement, labour migration, business relocation, changing logistics and investment patterns, and the need for post-war recovery. Yet the city lacks a comprehensive, up-to-date evidence base to understand these changes, identify emerging economic strengths and vulnerabilities, and make informed decisions about its future development.

The project aims to develop an integrated, evidence-based framework for analysing and shaping Lviv’s economy by combining economic, demographic, spatial, infrastructure and business data with stakeholder research. In close collaboration with Lviv City Council and an ETH-Domain research partner, the project will identify key growth drivers, barriers to growth and investment opportunities and investment in order to develop a methodology for prioritising sectors, policies and projects.

The project could provide a transferable approach for other cities facing major economic, demographic and spatial transformations caused by war, displacement or other systemic shocks.

The resulting evidence base become a strong and the most important base for Lviv’s Economic Development Strategy to 2030/2035 and serve as a practical tool for current and potential investors seeking reliable information on opportunities in Lviv as a strategically located, EU-border city and gateway to the Ukrainian market. Success will mean a validated methodology, clear economic priorities and actionable investment and development projects that strengthen the city’s resilience and competitiveness.
keywords: Lviv Economic Development,  Evidence-Based Urban Planning, Lviv's Economic Resilience Investment & Competitiveness, Post-War Urban Recovery
rationale: The ETH-domain researcher is crucial because the project requires a level of independent scientific expertise that is not currently available within the city’s existing analytical and consulting capacity. Lviv needs to move beyond descriptive economic analysis towards advanced spatial-economic modelling, integrated data analysis, scenario development and evidence-based forecasting to understand how war, displacement, migration, investment and infrastructure are reshaping its economy. An ETH-domain researcher from Switzerland would provide internationally recognised research methods, an independent perspective and expertise in modelling complex urban systems to support strategic decision-making.  This expertise would closely complement the work of Lviv’s business community, universities, civil society and the municipal institution City Institute, an established analytical and strategic-planning organisation. We have also held consultations with leading consulting companies specialising in strategic planning, which are ready to contribute to the project.
role: The Department of Economic Development of Lviv City Council would provide the researcher with access to municipal statistical and economic data, a comprehensive database of local businesses, and knowledge of the city’s economic context. We have already conducted preliminary analysis of existing sectoral strategies and strategies of other cities, and have established strong links with Lviv’s universities, research institutions, business community and the municipal Institute of the City.  Our role would be to facilitate data collection, stakeholder engagement, fieldwork and validation of research findings, ensuring that the research is grounded in Lviv’s real economic environment. Together, we aim to deliver a comprehensive economic study of Lviv Territorial Community, identifying growth sectors, economic vulnerabilities, labour and demographic trends, and infrastructure needs. The evidence generated would directly inform an actionable Economic Development Strategy for Lviv to 2030/2035 and evidence-based policies for investment, job creation, competitiveness and quality of life.

name: Open Cities Lab
title: Resilient municipal electricity through better data
summary: Municipal electricity teams often manage asset, inspection, maintenance, service-vehicle and expenditure data across separate systems, limiting their ability to prioritise preventative maintenance and allocate resources effectively. The project would ask: How can integrated municipal data improve asset and fleet management, maintenance decisions and service reliability in municipal electricity services? Working with Tshwane or the City of Johannesburg, we would develop and test a decision-support model that combines relevant operational and spatial data. The project would build on Open Cities Lab’s VoltManage product and electricity asset-management work with the City of Cape Town. Success would mean evidence that the approach improves maintenance prioritisation, vehicle deployment and investment planning, together with a reusable model that other municipalities could adopt. A private-sector implementation partner could subsequently help sustain and scale the solution beyond the initial research and pilot.
keywords: Municipal electricity; infrastructure asset management; preventative maintenance; fleet optimisation; data-driven decision-making
rationale: Open Cities Lab’s strength lies in practical, user-centred delivery with municipalities rather than academic research. An ETH researcher would therefore be essential to translate our operational experience into a rigorous research design, develop and validate appropriate models, and evaluate whether and under what conditions integrated data improves maintenance decisions and electricity-service reliability. We require expertise in energy and infrastructure systems, asset and fleet optimisation, applied data science and impact evaluation. This would ensure the project produces credible, transferable evidence alongside a practical solution that municipalities can use.
role: Open Cities Lab would bring practical experience in municipal data systems, electricity asset management, interoperability and user-centred digital tools, including lessons from VoltManage and our work with the City of Cape Town. We would help identify and engage a city partner, understand operational needs, facilitate appropriate data access, and lead the practical development, testing and adoption of the solution with municipal teams. We would also contribute data engineering, product development and stakeholder-engagement expertise. The ETH researcher would complement this with rigorous research design, infrastructure and energy expertise, modelling and impact evaluation. Together, we could produce both credible evidence and a practical, reusable solution, with a pathway for longer-term implementation and scaling through an appropriate private-sector partner.

name: Regional Development Agency of the Kyiv Region (RDAKR)
title: Prioritising Municipal Energy Investments under Wartime Uncertainty. A Decision-Support Method for Kyiv Oblast Communities
summary:
Kyiv Oblast communities must rehabilitate and build resilience of public infrastructure like hospitals, water utilities, schools, heat supply under attack-driven damage, blackout risk and displacement, with a pipeline of decentralised energy projects far exceeding available financing. Municipal leaders, residents and donors currently choose investments without an evidence-based, transparent rationale; SECAP planning assumes stable conditions and ignores security of supply.
     Objective is to co-create an evidence-based decision-support tool for prioritising decentralised energy investments in public infrastructure under wartime uncertainty, combining resilience, cost, emissions and social criteria, and a governance model for its use by municipalities and financiers.
     Approach lies in development and testing the tool with RDAKR's real portfolio of 22 energy projects from 16 communities, SECAPs for 10 communities, reconstruction context of Bucha and Borodianka — building on our SECO/Helvetas cooperation in Kyiv Oblast.
     Success covers a validated, digital, replicable tool adopted in SECAP recommendations and the Kyiv Oblast Development Strategy 2028–2034, scalable to other oblasts (regions).
keywords: decentralised energy management, resilient public infrastructure, evidence-based decision-support, urban governance, recovery and reconstruction
rationale: Our gap is methodological since we know which energy projects communities want, but not how to prioritise them defensibly when attack probabilities, blackout duration and donor flows cannot be forecast. Consultants apply standard cost-benefit or SECAP templates that assume stable conditions; day-to-day operations cannot test alternatives. Rigorous research can define measurable resilience criteria for public infrastructure, model decentralised energy options under deep uncertainty, and evaluate which prioritisation rules perform robustly across scenarios. We need expertise in energy systems modelling, decision analysis under uncertainty and infrastructure resilience — and the credibility an ETH-domain partner gives the tool with financiers and government.
role: energy systems and infrastructure resilience modelling, multi-criteria decision analysis under deep uncertainty, evaluation methods; ideally experience with municipal energy planning or digital decision-support tools.  RDAKR offers a ready empirical base and uptake channel. Data: a structured portfolio of 22 municipal energy projects from 16 communities with costing, ownership and documentation status; SECAPs for 10 communities (being developed under Interreg Europe GreenGov to 2028); a regional biogas potential study; the Kyiv Oblast investment catalogue. Field sites: partner communities including Bucha and Borodianka reconstruction areas, with direct access to hospitals, water and heat utilities through our founders — Kyiv Oblast Council and State Administration. Networks: 60+ oblast communities, regional government, Swiss cooperation (SECO/Helvetas project partner), and donor coordination. Contribution: staff time of our international projects team, workshops with municipalities, data collection and validation, translation, in-kind support. Policy uptake: integration into SECAP recommendations and the Kyiv Oblast Development Strategy 2028–2034.

name: Czech University of Life Sciences Prague
title: Biodiversity-Friendly Urban Lighting: From Light Pollution to Smart Night-Time Infrastructure
summary:
Artificial light at night is an increasing challenge for cities, affecting nocturnal biodiversity while also creating unnecessary energy consumption and environmental impacts. Cities need practical solutions that balance public safety, quality of urban space, energy efficiency and biodiversity protection.

We propose to develop and pilot a biodiversity-friendly approach to urban lighting that integrates ecological considerations into the planning, design and management of public lighting infrastructure. The project would combine ecological assessment, measurements of lighting characteristics and practical evaluation of different lighting strategies, including light intensity, spectrum, timing and spatial distribution. Pilot sites would be used to test interventions and evaluate their ecological and practical outcomes.

The goal is to develop a transferable, evidence-based approach that can support cities in planning, upgrading and managing public lighting infrastructure, demonstrating that efficient and functional night-time environments can be designed while substantially reducing impacts on biodiversity.
keywords: Artificial light at night (ALAN), urban biodiversity, public lighting, nature-positive infrastructure, smart cities
rationale: A researcher from the ETH domain is crucial for integrating rigorous ecological research with the practical challenges of urban lighting. The key knowledge gap is how specific lighting characteristics—spectrum, intensity, timing and spatial distribution—affect nocturnal biodiversity under realistic urban conditions. We require expertise in experimental design, biodiversity monitoring, light ecology and data analysis to identify effective interventions and quantify their ecological outcomes. This research-based approach will enable evidence-driven solutions that go beyond conventional lighting practice or consultancy and can be robustly tested, evaluated and transferred to other urban contexts.
role: The ideal researcher would bring expertise in artificial light at night, urban ecology and biodiversity, combined with strong skills in experimental design, light measurement, ecological monitoring and statistical modelling. Their role would be to co-design robust field experiments, evaluate ecological effects of different lighting strategies and help translate findings into evidence-based solutions for urban infrastructure.  We can contribute established expertise in insect ecology and ALAN, field experience with nocturnal arthropod monitoring, experimental protocols, light measurements and biodiversity datasets. We can also provide access to field sites, research equipment, staff time and established research networks. Together, the collaboration would connect ecological research with practical urban lighting challenges and support the development and testing of solutions that can be applied beyond individual pilot sites.

name: LCCE Lvivvodokanal
title: Smart and Resilient Urban Water Management through AI, GIS and Energy Optimisation
summary:
Lvivvodokanal serves more than one million people through a large and complex water supply system that faces ageing infrastructure, high energy consumption, limited digital integration and increasing resilience risks caused by power disruptions and other emergencies. These challenges affect service reliability, operational costs and the utility’s ability to prioritise investments effectively.

The project aims to develop and test a data-driven approach combining AI, GIS, asset data, hydraulic information and energy-use data to improve infrastructure management and operational resilience.

The proposed approach includes failure-risk prediction, prioritisation of rehabilitation measures, optimisation of pumping and energy use, and modelling of water-supply performance during power disruptions.

Success would mean a validated decision-support approach tested on selected Lvivvodokanal assets, measurable improvements in planning and operational efficiency, and a scalable methodology that could later be replicated by other Ukrainian water utilities.
keywords: Urban water management; Artificial Intelligence (AI); GIS; Asset management; Energy optimisation
rationale: Lvivvodokanal has strong operational expertise and access to real-world infrastructure data, but we need advanced research capacity to transform these data into scientifically validated decision-support methods. An ETH Domain researcher is essential to help develop robust AI, GIS, hydraulic and energy-modelling approaches, define appropriate research methodology, and validate results beyond routine operational analysis. This expertise would allow us to identify patterns, risks and optimisation opportunities that cannot be reliably derived through day-to-day utility operations alone. We are particularly seeking expertise in urban water systems, data science/AI, infrastructure asset management, hydraulic modelling, energy optimisation and resilience assessment.
role: Lvivvodokanal can offer a unique real-world testing environment for applied research in urban water infrastructure. We can provide access to operational and historical data, GIS and asset information, selected pumping stations and network areas, technical documentation, and support from experienced utility staff. Our team can contribute practical knowledge of water-system operation, energy use, infrastructure failures, emergency response and investment planning.  We expect the ETH researcher to bring advanced expertise in urban water systems, AI/data analytics, GIS, hydraulic and energy modelling, asset management, resilience assessment and scientific validation methods. The collaboration would combine academic rigor with operational practice, allowing new methods to be tested under real utility conditions. Lvivvodokanal can also support field validation, staff time, access to facilities and in-kind contributions, and help adapt the results for replication by other Ukrainian water utilities.

name: Office for European Integration and Development
title: Circular Sludge: Wastewater Sludge Treatment and Resource Recovery
summary:
The project aims to establish a modern system for managing sludge generated during wastewater treatment in the Ivano-Frankivsk community. Currently, sludge accumulation and disposal require significant resources, create additional pressure on infrastructure and pose potential environmental risks.
The project will assess the composition and volumes of sludge generated, develop a techno-economic feasibility study and implement a pilot treatment technology. Depending on laboratory research and techno-economic analysis, potential approaches may include anaerobic treatment, drying, composting, hydrothermal carbonisation or other modern methods that can transform sludge from waste into a resource.
The ultimate goal is to reduce the amount of sludge requiring disposal, decrease environmental impacts and management costs, and recover useful products such as biogas/energy, stabilised organic material and potentially valuable nutrients, including phosphorus and nitrogen. The pilot will support Ivano-Frankivsk's transition towards a circular model of water and waste management, with potential for replication across Ukrainian communities
keywords: Circular economy; wastewater sludge; resource recovery; wastewater management; environmental sustainability
rationale: The project requires research expertise to determine the most appropriate and sustainable pathway for transforming wastewater sludge into a useful resource. A researcher from the ETH domain could provide expertise in environmental engineering, sludge treatment technologies, resource recovery, laboratory analysis, techno-economic assessment and environmental impact evaluation. Rigorous research is needed to determine which treatment technology is technically feasible, environmentally safe and economically viable for the specific conditions of Ivano-Frankivsk. The research should provide the evidence needed to select and pilot an appropriate technology rather than relying on a generic technological solution
role: The Office can facilitate cooperation with the municipal water utility and relevant city departments and provide access to the local context and available information on sludge generation, wastewater treatment and existing infrastructure. We can support the organization of field and laboratory activities, collection of relevant operational data and identification of a suitable pilot site. The Office can also facilitate engagement with municipal decision-makers and other local stakeholders, support the development of the techno-economic feasibility study and help translate research results into a practical municipal solution. We can further support the identification of potential funding opportunities and the future scaling of the pilot model to other Ukrainian communities

name: ETE Institute (Open Source Europe)
countries: Ghana; Kyrgyzstan; Peru; South Africa; Romania; Vietnam; Egypt
title: ÉTÈ: Neuromorphic & Geometric Safety Infrastructure for High-Risk Physical AI & Urban Resilience
summary:
Urban operators, drone fleets, and industrial workers face mounting safety risks from AI unreliability and unstandardized cross-border data. ÉTÈ addresses this by deploying a deterministic 6D geometric and neuromorphic safety kernel ("The Amygdala") to provide microsecond hard-stopping and compliance for high-risk physical AI.

Collaborating with European research and OGC spatial standards, our objective is to operationalize a "defatigue/cognitive load" safety architecture in urban IoT and low-altitude economies.
